title: Revision clarifies a principle’s basis

captions.physics: Examining a shared explanation’s inadequate foundation

meaning: Examining inadequate foundations can reveal a more substantial basis and bring trust in a principle that has become more understandable together.
text: Trust in a principle can change after a ready explanation is lost. The Tower in the physical position of Ajna suggests jointly examining a conclusion’s inadequate foundation. The Tower in energy supports seeking firmer grounds beyond familiar appearances. The Hierophant in emotions trusts an understood principle. Losing a simple answer may feel difficult. Joint action reveals its limit while constructive motive seeks what actually connects with material for both people.

For example, you thought an understandable rule must stay identical across every case. Comparing two explainable exceptions, you stop treating invariability as a sufficient measure of value. **Revision can restore trust in substantially understood foundations.** Seeking actual grounds reveals conditions of application. A principle gains another meaning: a relationship remains within named boundaries. Trust rests on understanding why particular cases differ. You can explain this while preserving questions without requiring a first general formulation to cover the entire variety of both people’s experience beforehand.

The risk is treating every refinement as proof of a principle’s complete failure while seeking firm foundations. Constructive inquiry distinguishes a narrow formulation from the relationship itself. Discovered boundaries concern a particular conclusion. Your view stays substantial when trust permits refinement, allowing each person to name foundations without dismantling all understanding whenever another detail appears.
